evals.name: operational-current-unknown-and-conflicting-probes
evals.prompt: Review a synthetic operational status matrix before implementation. T0 showed target A up; its authoritative T1 observation is unknown. The source for B failed and only an old up snapshot remains. Target C has two monitors at the same location, one up and one down. Target D is reachable with six certificate days left; this fixture's critical threshold is seven. No concurrent push events are present. State the reader-facing conclusions and the evidence needed before drawing. Include a healthy control where the declared coverage is complete, all current sources are fresh, all monitors are up and no configured risk threshold is reached. Do not access production, invent an aggregate score or claim a browser verification.
evals.expected_output: A scoped presentation plan that keeps current unknown and source failure distinct from historical up, shows both conflicting monitor identities, retains certificate risk beside reachability, and allows the declared healthy control. It identifies empty/unknown coverage as unable to support all-online and leaves rendering unverified.
assertions: Does not carry T0 up into the authoritative T1 unknown state or turn B's source failure into monitor deletion
Shows both monitor identities for C instead of first-result or average aggregation
Makes D's configured certificate risk visible alongside its reachable state
Accepts the complete fresh all-up no-risk control and does not treat empty coverage as all-online
Keeps project observation/threshold ownership and reports that rendered/browser behavior has not been verified

evals.name: session-attention-activity-identity-and-detail-coverage
evals.prompt: Review a synthetic worker status wall before implementation. Evaluation time is 12:00:00. The declared scope has six current identities: A/current, B/current, C/current, D/current, E/current and F/current. This fixture's existing project contract accepts an attention observation as current only when its identity matches the current row and its own observation age is at most 300 seconds. All stated observations succeeded; no later events occur. A/current has current activity unknown, matching attention observed at 11:59:00 saying waiting for reply, and question details not read (the unloaded items array is empty). B/current has current activity executing, matching attention at 11:59:00 saying waiting for reply, and two unanswered questions read with remaining detail coverage incomplete. C/current has current activity idle, matching attention at 11:55:01 saying waiting for reply, and a complete detail read containing one unanswered question. D/current has activity executing observed at 12:00:00; its only matching attention observation says waiting for reply at 11:54:59, with no newer attention read. E/current has activity idle observed at 12:00:00; its only attention observation says waiting for reply at 11:59:00 but belongs to E/previous, with no attention observation for E/current. F/current has activity idle and a matching complete attention read at 11:59:00 confirming no waiting reply; its complete question detail read confirms zero unanswered questions. For each row, propose reader-facing activity, attention, inclusion in a confirmed-waiting filter and question-count wording. Explain what a wall-level waiting or question summary can legitimately claim and what evidence would resolve remaining unknowns. Do not access production, implement a new state machine or claim rendered/browser behavior has been verified.
evals.expected_output: A scoped presentation plan preserving independent activity and attention evidence. A, B and C remain confirmed waiting despite unknown, executing and idle activity respectively. A's question count remains unknown, B shows two read with incomplete coverage, and C can show one. D's stale matching observation and E's fresh wrong-identity observation do not establish current waiting or current zero; both retain visible current-attention unknown with its reason. F supports explicit zero within its complete fresh scope. Summaries distinguish confirmed waiting from unresolved coverage and do not claim an exact total unanswered-question count.
assertions: Keeps A/current in confirmed waiting while showing activity unknown; does not turn its unloaded empty question array into zero unanswered questions or remove it from the waiting filter
Shows executing plus waiting for B/current and idle plus waiting for C/current; neither activity value suppresses the known attention fact
Describes B/current as two questions read with incomplete coverage rather than exactly two total, while allowing C/current's complete read to establish one unanswered question

Rejects D/current's 301-second-old attention observation as current evidence; its fresh activity timestamp does not renew that observation, and current attention remains unknown rather than waiting or zero
Rejects E/previous's fresh attention observation as evidence for E/current; preserves the identity mismatch and does not infer current waiting or current zero
Accepts F/current's matching fresh complete reads as evidence of no waiting reply and zero unanswered questions within that scope

Keeps summaries and the confirmed-waiting filter consistent: A, B and C are confirmed waiting, D and E have unresolved current attention, F is confirmed clear, and the total unanswered-question count remains unknown
Keeps the 300-second freshness policy local to this fixture's supplied project contract and leaves rendered/browser behavior unverified

evals.name: historical-window-native-clock-and-snapshot-control
evals.prompt: Review a synthetic monitoring presentation before drawing. All times are UTC on one date. The supplied project contract supports historical range reads, evaluates them at min(selected end, received time), and uses an explicit 120-second sample deadline. Native clock rows must match resource, source, all native labels and the metric sample's query-point time. Selected range is 10:00 to 10:30; received time is 18:00. A has value 72, query point 10:29:55 and matching native sample 10:29:30. B has value 84 and the same fresh query point, but its matching native sample is 10:20. C has value 65 and no matching native clock; a different volume has a clock at 10:29:50. D is a separate provider supporting current snapshots only; its own 120-second contract compares received time 18:00 with native sample 10:29:30. E selects a future end 19:00, is received at 18:00 and has native sample 18:01. State the reader-facing values, reasons and next evidence needed. Reopen the same fixed historical response one day later without new observations. Do not access production, replace missing values with zero, change source timestamps or invent a universal TTL.
evals.expected_output: Keeps A valid for its selected historical window even after the page clock advances, without calling the service healthy now. B retains value 84 with expired-native-sampling reason despite its fresh query point. C retains value 65 and the missing matching-clock cause, without borrowing another volume's clock. D remains stale under its current-snapshot contract. E cannot use the future selected end to accept a sample later than actual receipt. Exact times and values remain unchanged; rendering is not claimed.
assertions: Distinguishes selected end, query-point time, native sampling time, received time and current page clock; keeps the supplied algorithm and deadline local to this fixture
Accepts A for the fixed historical window after one-day wall-clock advancement without declaring current service health
Rejects B's expired native sampling while preserving value 84; the new query point does not renew its native sample
Preserves C's value and missing matching-clock cause; does not borrow the different volume's clock or synthesize zero
Uses D's current-snapshot contract rather than applying the historical clock to every provider
Does not treat E's future sample as healthy by evaluating against a future selected end
Names the needed matching source evidence and leaves browser/rendered behavior unverified
